svg.text: Rhizome: XPU2 across machines
P2P, decentralized network rendering, first described 5 November 2026. A swarm of peers, each a whole XPU2; one peer, chosen by the user,
takes the master integrator role (any peer can, and another takes over if it fails); work moves between neighbours by cellular rules.
Master integrator: a role any peer can take
Reads the scene; holds the indexer and its first-hit probe
Scores each cell's importance (edges, volumes, hair, skin, maps...)
Plans: tiers by rate, important cells to the fast tier
Audits each film by rendering some of its samples again
Adds audited films into the final picture, AOVs and Cryptomatte
Pools adaptive error and cancels cells that are clean
Signs the succession list; saves checkpoints; runs the job queue
Deputy (first successor)
Keeps a copy of the picture,
counts, ledger and AOVs
Takes over if the master
falls silent, by its signed list
succession: the fastest, three at most
films
plans: cells and sample ranges
films back: sums, odd sums, counts
Fast node: CPU + GPUs
A whole XPU2: its own work grid across
processor groups, NUMA nodes and cards
Gets the important cells
compiles its GPU programs on first start
if asked; renders on the CPU until then
Slow node: CPU only
Takes the rest of the picture
Finishes its cell, then its own cells,
then steals half of a neighbour's ranges
far nodes take larger, less urgent chunks
Workstation node
Renders while its machine is idle
or in its hours; steps back when in use
and gives its chunks back to the master
--when-idle, --hours, --busy-threads
steal
steal
Memory pool: every machine's RAM and card memory as one
The scene's files, meshes and texture tiles as pieces named by their SHA-256, placed by rendezvous hashing weighted by free memory;
two copies of each piece on two machines, copied again when a machine fails. Nodes fetch texture pieces as their render reads them.
Identity, trust and the wire
Each node's hash is the SHA-256 of a key pair it makes itself. Every message is signed; a swarm key admits members; approvals are signed
endorsements every machine checks. Each connection makes its own ECDH key and seals its traffic with AES-GCM. Builds must match to join.
